does: Softens dried rice noodles in warm water until they bend but are still firm at the core, so that they finish cooking in the wok.
how: Put the noodles in a large bowl and cover with warm water from the tap, not boiling.
Leave them until they are soft and bendy but still white and firm in the middle.
Drain them well and toss with a little oil so that they do not stick.

cues.text: A noodle bends around your finger but still has a firm core when bitten.
The strands turn from glassy to opaque white.

mistakes.mistake: Soaking in boiling water or for too long, so the noodles turn mushy and break in the wok.
mistakes.fix: Use warm water and drain while they are still firm.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving drained noodles to sit, so they glue together.
mistakes.fix: Toss them with a little oil.

variant_of.differs: The soak is short and in warm water, and stops while the noodles are still firm so that the wok finishes them.
